title: The Shattered Halls
body: The Shattered Halls lie at the heart of Hellfire Citadel, behind a door the fel orcs keep locked, and they belong to the Shattered Hand clan and its chieftain, Kargath Bladefist, who calls himself warchief of the Fel Horde. The halls are given over to war. Gladiators spar under the eyes of centurions, houndmasters keep rabid warhounds, assassins wait in the shadows, and in one long hall a blood guard drills archers to loose burning arrows down its length on his command. Shadowmoon acolytes and darkcasters serve beside the warriors, and everywhere the same cries ring out: the blood is our power, ours is the true Horde, for Kargath and for victory. Kargath's lieutenants hold chambers of their own on the way to the warchief's hall. Honor Hold and Thrallmar alike want Kargath dead.

title: Grand Warlock Nethekurse
body: Grand Warlock Nethekurse, a fel orc warlock, holds a chamber in the Shattered Halls where he amuses himself by tormenting his own kind. Fel orc converts wait in his chamber, and he tries his spells on them, searing them, coiling death about them and cracking the ground beneath their feet, while they wail that their skin is on fire. Two strange braziers burn beside him, and the fel embers inside them lend his magic its power. When intruders arrive, he is happy to let them finish his work for him.

parts.body: Nethekurse met the intruders with mockery, whether they cut down his converts one by one or tried to fight them all at once. Then he fought them himself, cleaving with shadow and splitting the ground beneath their feet, and when hard pressed he spun in a storm of darkness. It was not enough. He died with a sigh: what a shame.
sources: creature_text 16807 groups 0 (You wish to fight us all at once?, if engaged before the converts are dead), 1-3 (converts handed over and mocked), 8 (What... a shame.)

parts.body: One of his fel embers was carried out of the halls to Magus Zabraxis at Honor Hold. She has no hope of matching Nethekurse's feats, she admits, and should not want to, but she would be a fool to ignore what the embers can do, and she means to study them in secret, for there are those who would forbid such research.

title: Warbringer O'mrogg
body: Warbringer O'mrogg is a two-headed ogre who fights for the Fel Horde in the Shattered Halls, and his two heads agree on almost nothing. The left is always hungry, quick to grow bored, and given to offering foes their lives if they are nice to him. The right is sharper and sour, tired of doing all the hard work and of being fat because his twin is never full. They squabble over whom to kill next even in the middle of a fight, and still they swing hard enough to make the quarrel dangerous to anyone close by.

parts.body: Even dying, the two heads could not agree. The left spent its last breath blaming its twin, insisting that this was all his fault. For once the right head had no answer ready, and the warbringer crashed to the floor of his chamber with the quarrel left unfinished.
sources: creature_text 19523 group 8 (This all... your fault!)

title: Warchief Kargath Bladefist
body: Kargath Bladefist, chieftain of the Shattered Hand, wears a blade where one hand should be, and he rules the Shattered Halls as warchief of the Fel Horde, a title no one granted him but himself. Long ago, while Ner'zhul worked to open the rifts that would tear Draenor apart, Kargath was left behind at Hellfire Citadel to hold off the Alliance. The fortress fell, and he escaped swearing he would one day take it back. He has. Now his army of crazed fel orcs means to see Thrallmar destroyed, and he proclaims his the true Horde and himself the only warchief. Thrall has ordered him defeated at all costs, and Danath Trollbane wants his weapon brought to Honor Hold.

parts.body: Kargath met the intruders with a warrior's boast, and fresh fighters kept pouring into the hall through a portal to fight beside him, while assassins rose from the shadows at its edges. It was not enough. The self-made warchief fell in his own hall, insisting with his last breath that the true Horde would prevail.
sources: creature_text 16808 groups 0 (aggro: one of three boasts), 2 (The true Horde... will prevail.)
boss_warchief_kargath_bladefist.cpp (four Shattered Hand Assassins summoned on engage; the Warchief's Portal 17611 summons Heathen, Reaver and Sharpshooter guards during the fight)

parts.body: Nazgrel took the news of his death without triumph. In his prime, he said, Kargath had been a fine warrior, a hero and an example to his people, and his fall was a blow to all of them, above all to Thrall. Whatever happened to him at the end, the orcs should remember the one he once was, and the lessons of his downfall.
sources: quest 9495 reward text

parts.body: Danath Trollbane took Kargath's fist as proof that a major blow had been struck against the orcs. The Sons of Lothar once believed their blood had bought Honor Hold its safety; now, reinforced at last, they meant to do far more than defend it, and to keep the orcs on the defensive.

title: The Shattered Hand's Key
body: At the Ata'mal Terrace in Shadowmoon Valley, Smith Gorlunk carried a freshly cast mold, meant for making a key of some sort. Whoever takes it from him finds an image engraved on its back that seems to belong to Hellfire Citadel, far away across Outland on the peninsula. That makes it worth showing to the commanders who face that fortress every day: Force Commander Danath Trollbane at Honor Hold, or Nazgrel, who leads the Horde's forces at Thrallmar. What such a key might open, and whether it can be made at all, is for them to judge.

parts.body: Looking closer, the commander recognized the symbol on the key's handle as the Shattered Hand's own: there was a good chance the key would open the Shattered Halls. The mold went on to the outpost's master smith, Dumphry at Honor Hold or Rohok at Thrallmar, for if anyone could forge such a key, he could.
sources: quests 10762 and 10756 descriptions (offered on turning in 10754/10755: RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: Fel iron alone would serve in such a mold, and no forge of coal burned hot enough to temper it. The only fire fierce enough was the scalding fel fire at the heart of a Legion fel reaver, so the mold had to be plunged into the remains of one, brought down in Hellfire Peninsula by those bold enough to try.
sources: quests 10763 and 10757 descriptions (only fel iron can be used with this mold)
quests 10764 and 10758 descriptions (not enough heat; the insides of the Legion's fel reavers; scalding core of fel fire)

parts.body: The charred mold gave up a working key, and the smith pronounced the work a success. All that was left was to carry it to Hellfire Citadel and try it on the locked door of the Shattered Halls, and there, Dumphry added, kill some orcs.

title: Pride of the Fel Horde
body: Honor Hold and Thrallmar know precious little about the Fel Horde inside Hellfire Citadel, and what they know was bought with many lives. Kargath Bladefist's troops are brutal and battle-hardened, fortified by foul magic. Their elite, the Shattered Hand legionnaires, centurions and champions, are feared by the rank and file and lead them as an officer corps. Field Commander Romus at Honor Hold and Shadow Hunter Ty'jin at Thrallmar agree on where any assault on the Fel Horde's leadership must begin: with those officers, hunted down in the Shattered Halls. Whatever Overlord Hun Maimfist may say of them, Ty'jin warns, this Fel Horde is nothing to be trifled with.

parts.body: Romus was no fool about it. The fall of the legionnaires did not mean victory over the Fel Horde, he admitted, but it was a good first step, and with progress to report from the citadel, Honor Hold could perhaps begin to turn its attention to the Fel Horde elsewhere in the peninsula and across Outland.
sources: quest 9493 completion text (I am not so naive as to think that the defeat of the Shattered Hand legionnaires heralds our victory, but is a good first step) and reward text (turn our attention to the Fel Horde presence in other parts of the peninsula and Outland)

parts.body: To Ty'jin, breaking the legionnaires meant the Fel Horde would be easier to face on the battlefield. He did not pretend the war had been won by it: even with its officers broken, the Fel Horde remained a formidable enemy, and Thrallmar would go on fighting it.

title: Kargath's Prisoners
body: Kargath Bladefist keeps prisoners in the Shattered Halls, soldiers of Honor Hold or Thrallmar taken in the fighting, and he means to put them to death. A fellow captive met inside warns that the executions are near, and that an important officer is among the condemned: Captain Alina of the Alliance, or Captain Boneshatter of the Horde. Should intruders press too deep into his fortress, the warchief means to have the prisoners brought out and the executioner called, so that they pay for the trespass with their lives. In Shattrath, A'dal knows of them too, and would see the executioner's axe come back without a drop of blood on its blade.

parts.body: Captain Alina was saved before the executioner could reach her, and she admitted she had never expected a rescue party to come. She set about gathering the rest of the prisoners to lead them home to Honor Hold.
sources: quest 9524 reward text

parts.body: Captain Boneshatter was saved before the executioner's blow could fall, and he was glad of it, though not because he feared to die. When death comes for him, he swore, it will find him on the battlefield, covered in the blood of his enemies and taking them down with him.
sources: quest 9525 reward text

parts.body: The executioner's axe was carried to A'dal unused, not a drop of blood on its blade, and with it the proof that Kargath's prisoners had been spared. The naaru declared the trial of mercy passed.
